result: No exact or gain-normalized duplicates found in the 301-program fixed-fixture screen. Focused checks distinguish the three strongest near pairs through register response, decay or onset.
bank_snapshot: 2026.11.1 after first level-calibration pass; root may subsequently adjust master levels
quantization_note: Each stereo sample is divided by the entire clip peak, multiplied by 1e6 and rounded to int32. This is a labelled numerical screen, not an acoustic or listening threshold.

focused_findings.observation: Similarity at MIDI 60 does not persist across register. At MIDI 84, held-body waveform correlation is 0.96805 and Contour Bass is 1.460 dB louder, compared with −0.075 dB relative level at MIDI 36. This is consistent with the deliberately different contour/filter voicing.

Both intentionally use 4-foot sine bodies with 2-foot attack partials. At MIDI 60, the revised Kalimba held body is 6.565 dB below Celesta after 2.8–3.0 seconds despite nearly equal immediate onset RMS (+0.020 dB). The body/upper decay and release values differ.

Both deliberately share a 16-foot sine foundation; only Sine Bass has the disappearing pulse click. At MIDI 48, the onset correlation is 0.99538 with a −20.36 dB fitted residual, while the 50–150 ms body correlation is 0.999964. The distinction is concentrated in the onset as described.

limitations: A single held note cannot establish full musical or perceptual distinctness.
Slow swells may not reach their body within this short fixture; fixed ring carriers and modulation depend on note and phrase history.
Near-identical fundamentals alone are not duplicate sounds; envelopes, pressure response, registration and modulation are reviewed separately.
Waveform/envelope/spectral similarity is a diagnostic ranking, not a perceptual quality score. No claim that all 301 programs are equally distinguishable in every playing situation is made.
This was not a listening-panel review. No program change is justified solely by a high correlation between intentionally related variants.
